opening.argument: The speaker discusses a reported Goldman Sachs condition for taking companies public: a company must have at least one woman or non-white board member. The discussion evaluates that policy, including a concern that it might violate gender discrimination laws and a view that board diversity can bring a unique perspective. A displayed news article provides context. The suggestion that a board member could claim a different identity is hypothetical criticism of how the condition might be skirted, not an observed offer, instruction, or confirmed attempt. Nothing in the material solicits money, credentials, investment participation, or a deceptive transaction.

citations.quote: The investment bank will refuse to take a company public unless it has at least one woman or non-white board member.
